A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BaNk-UCB research work. Their text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reformatting and removal of the lower-bound proof.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendix C.1 report original simulations and classification-bandit experiments, including cumulative regret and incorrect-action rates.

after.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendix B.1 retain the original simulation and real-data experimental results.

M1.justification: Equation 6 changes the neighborhood-selection threshold from ln(t_{m-1})/j to sqrt(ln(t_{m-1})/j). This localized correction agrees with the square-root calculation already present in v1's Lemma 5. The overall k-NN UCB and batching framework is retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two synthetic settings at dimensions 2–5 and the same Rice, Occupancy Detection, and EEG Eye State datasets. V2's spherical and manifold-shaped domain examples are explanatory discussion, not additional evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: BaSEDB remains the sole evaluated comparator in every synthetic, real-data, and higher-dimensional experiment. Newly citing Guan and Jiang (2018) does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Reported protocols remain unchanged: synthetic experiments use T = 10000, L = 1, and five batches; real-data experiments retain the same sample counts, binary rewards, and respective batch counts of 3, 4, and 6. Both methods still share batch grids. The PDFs do not report rerunning experiments following the formula correction.

E4.justification: The dimension-sensitivity experiments and their discussion move from Appendix C.1 to B.1 without substantive changes. No new ablations, scheduling-sensitivity experiments, robustness tests, or case studies are reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report 30 independent simulation runs, 30 random dataset permutations for real-data evaluation, and uncertainty bands of ±1.96 standard errors. No seed information or statistical estimation procedure is added or changed.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 retain identical experimental plot content, including regret and incorrect-action curves, uncertainty bands, and the reported advantage over BaSEDB. No empirical result entries are added, removed, or numerically revised.

T1.justification: V2 removes the entire Appendix C lower-bound derivation, including Lemmas 11–13 and the associated inferior-sampling-rate machinery. Theorem 2 retains its bound but is now presented as a result of Jiang and Ma (2025). The upper-bound theorem, assumptions, and supporting proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces adaptation to context dimension with adaptation to context density. The conclusion also explicitly characterizes scheduling robustness as empirical. The central minimax-rate and empirical-superiority claims are retained.

C2.justification: V2 more explicitly identifies intrinsic-dimension adaptation and guarantees under arbitrary batch schedules as open problems, and adds exclusions concerning fairness and distribution-shift robustness. It drops v1's explicit known-Lipschitz-constant limitation from the conclusion, although L remains in the algorithm.

D1.justification: V1's Section 3 specifies log(T)/|A| initial pure-exploration samples; v2 omits this instruction and newly states that action ties are broken arbitrarily. These change implementation documentation without establishing what initialization was actually used in the unchanged experiments.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly describes BaNk-UCB as a batched extension of Zhao et al. (2024), attributes Theorem 2 directly to Jiang and Ma (2025), and adds a comparative remark explaining the batch-wise upper-bound contribution. These refine previously acknowledged relationships. Guan and Jiang (2018) is added, while Tsybakov (2009) disappears with the lower-bound proof.

P1.justification: V2 expands selected introductory, geometric, and methodological explanations, rewrites the limitations paragraph, and adds a comparison remark and Broader Impact Statement. The appendix organization changes following proof removal, but the main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively retypeset with different title and author formatting, fonts, heading styles, margins, and running rules. Figures are enlarged and repositioned: Figures 1 and 2 now share a page, while Figure 3 becomes larger and top-aligned. Their experimental content and panel arrangements remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves internal consistency through the Equation 6 correction, narrows adaptation claims, and clarifies attribution. Removing Appendix C also removes v1's invalid finite-KL argument for Bern(h) versus Bern(0) in Lemma 12. These gains are tempered by lost initialization documentation and the dropped known-L caveat. The empirical evidence and upper-bound analysis are otherwise essentially unchanged.
